name: Mamata Banerjee
role: Indian politician; Chief Minister of West Bengal 2011-2026 and founder-leader of the Trinamool Congress; also Union Railway Minister (1999-2000, 2009-2011)
summary: Banerjee is a populist, welfare-oriented politician of the Bengali centre-left who rose by opposing forcible farmland acquisition at Singur and Nandigram. She backs wide cash-transfer and health schemes, legal crop price guarantees and a strong federal role for states, and opposes the CAA, NRC and a Uniform Civil Code while stressing communal harmony. She courts industry, favours rapid growth and tough punishment for rape, and accuses the BJP-led Centre of undermining federalism and democracy.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent third-model audit; full blank list and all 490 statements reviewed. No existing answers were read. Most effort went to new full interviews, Bengali sources, ideology, technology and foreign policy. The ten prioritized items yield three program-based answers: national rebirth, sacred nation and homeland spiritual bond. They rest on the complete official Maa Mati Manush vision, corroborated and contextualized by the scholarly study, not on an assumption from nationalism. In the town hall she explicitly names Maa Mati Manush as her party’s ideology. The page has no personal byline: these are medium, modest-strength program positions under her founder leadership, not claims of personal authorship or private religious beliefs. The scholar’s interpretations, followers’ praise and hostile critics are separated from the primary program. This source warrants integrator attention because its mystical national language is stronger than her pluralist interview wording; the two concern different claims and do not imply religiously restricted citizenship. Convergence of left and right in her 2011 description of her party does not explicitly declare the division obsolete; left-right-obsolete remains null. Pro-industry welfare policy does not establish class collaboration, abolition of wages, Marxist history or rejection of capitalism and communism alike. Her latest election refusal is included as mixed evidence without accepting either her fraud claim or the BJP’s characterization as proven. Cartoon-arrest defense controls the opposition-suppression answer despite public assurances of dissent. No genetic racial claims or compulsory religious rules are inferred. Her nephew’s recruitment is not succession to state office by a child. Kashmir’s Article 370 exchange explicitly withholds a policy commitment and is not scored as minority autonomy. Gorkhaland allegations concern partition of West Bengal rather than breaking up India, so foreign-partition-plot stays null. The UN peacekeeper demand supplies a concrete humanitarian deployment position, not blanket advocacy of invasions or increased UN power. Her 2025 coal project supplies a current fossil expansion record despite environmental concern in 2014; no drastic-climate-action score is invented. Employment protection in her Bengali AI remarks is distinguished from technical optimism, algorithmic government and enhancement. Avoiding job losses does not establish opposition to reducing work hours through automation, so automate-paid-work remains null. General food choice does not establish a position on cattle slaughter specifically. Her “100 days work” scheme does not establish a universal job guarantee; allowances do not establish universal basic income. No inferred answers.
